epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. The export contains one row per paid order with order number, order date and total amount including VAT. Cancelled orders are excluded. The file is UTF-8 without BOM, semicolon-delimited, with a header row, and is named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv where the date is the export date in Europe/Paris.

features.description: Customer capability to download a CSV file listing their paid orders from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a logged-in customer on the account page, When they trigger the order export, Then a CSV file is downloaded to their device
Given a customer with paid and cancelled orders, When they export their orders, Then only the paid orders are present in the file
Given a customer with no logged-in session, When they try to access the export, Then no export file is provided
stories.aiReadyReason: The story is implementable: the export action on the account page, the paid-order filter (captured payment, not fully refunded, per the glossary), and the no-session rejection are all specified and testable.
stories.description: The account page offers an action that downloads a CSV file containing the paid orders of the logged-in customer. Only paid orders are included, so cancelled orders are excluded. A paid order is an order whose payment is captured and which is not fully refunded.
stories.iWant: to export my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep a record of my purchases

tasks.description: Add a backend query that selects the logged-in customer's paid orders (payment captured and not fully refunded) and excludes cancelled orders. Generate the CSV as UTF-8 without BOM, semicolon-delimited, with a header row, dates as YYYY-MM-DD and amounts with a dot and two decimals. Expected result: the service returns only paid orders of that customer in the required CSV format.
tasks.title: Implement paid orders query and CSV generation

tasks.description: Add an API action that returns the generated CSV as a downloadable file for an authenticated customer. Expected result: an authenticated request returns the CSV file with a download disposition.
tasks.title: Expose authenticated export endpoint

tasks.description: Ensure the export action rejects requests without a logged-in session and returns no file content, and that each export only contains the orders of the session's customer. Expected result: unauthenticated requests receive no export file and customers never receive other customers' orders.
tasks.title: Enforce access control on the export

tasks.description: Add an action on the account page that triggers the export request and downloads the returned CSV file to the customer's device. Expected result: a logged-in customer clicking the action gets the CSV file downloaded.
tasks.title: Add export action to account page

tasks.description: Write automated tests verifying that a logged-in customer receives a downloaded CSV, that cancelled orders are absent while paid orders are present, and that an unauthenticated request yields no export file. Expected result: all three acceptance criteria of the story pass.
tasks.title: Test paid orders export acceptance criteria

stories.title: Download paid orders CSV from account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with three paid orders, When the export file is generated, Then the file contains a header row followed by exactly three data rows, one per order
Given a paid order, When it is exported, Then its row contains the order number, the order date formatted YYYY-MM-DD and the total amount including VAT with a dot and two decimals
Given a customer with a cancelled order, When the export file is generated, Then no row corresponds to the cancelled order
Given a paid order that has been partially refunded, When the export file is generated, Then the order still appears as one row
Given the export file, When it is opened, Then it is encoded in UTF-8 without BOM, uses a semicolon as delimiter and has a header row
stories.aiReadyReason: The story does not say whether the total amount of a partially refunded order is the original total including VAT or the total net of the refund, so the amount in the export is ambiguous: should the exported total for a partially refunded paid order be the original total including VAT or the amount net of the refund?
dependencies: Download paid orders CSV from account page
stories.description: Each paid order produces exactly one data row with its order number, its order date and its total amount including VAT. Dates use the format YYYY-MM-DD and amounts use a dot as decimal separator with two decimals. The file is UTF-8 without BOM, uses a semicolon as delimiter and has a header row. A paid order that is partially refunded remains in the export.
stories.iWant: the exported file to contain one row per paid order with order number, date and total amount including VAT in a UTF-8 semicolon-delimited CSV with a header row
stories.soThat: I can read my order history in a spreadsheet
stories.title: Export one row per paid order with order number, date and total

acceptanceCriteria: Given an export made on 2024-03-15 in Europe/Paris time, When the file is downloaded, Then its name is orders-2024-03-15.csv
Given an export made just after midnight in Europe/Paris time, When the file is downloaded, Then the date in the file name is the Europe/Paris date of the export
stories.aiReadyReason: The file name pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv and the Europe/Paris export date rule are fully specified and match the project context, with clear verifiable examples.
dependencies: Download paid orders CSV from account page
stories.description: The downloaded file is named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where the date is the date of the export in the Europe/Paris time zone.
stories.iWant: the exported file to be named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv with the date of the export
stories.soThat: I can identify when my export was made

tasks.description: Compute the export date in the Europe/Paris time zone at the moment of the export and set the downloaded file name to orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. Expected result: the file name uses the Europe/Paris date, including for exports made just after midnight Paris time.
tasks.title: Set export file name with Europe/Paris date

tasks.description: Write automated tests verifying that an export made on 2024-03-15 Paris time is named orders-2024-03-15.csv and that an export made just after midnight Paris time uses the Paris date. Expected result: both acceptance criteria of the story pass.
tasks.title: Test export file name acceptance criteria

stories.title: Name export file with export date
